dosing.evidence: Ayahuasca was diluted in filtered water and administered by gavage at doses of 2.5, 7.5, 12.5 or 15 mg DMT/kg

group_housing.evidence: Animals were housed in plastic cages (no per-cage number specified)

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12:12 h light/dark cycle (lights on at 7:00 a.m.)

assays.assay_description: Three-chamber CPP apparatus (44 × 14 × 14 cm) with two distinct end-chambers (different walls and floors) and a small grey middle chamber. Used across three protocols: (I) ayahuasca dose-response CPP (2.5–15 mg DMT/kg), (II) cocaine vs. ayahuasca choice-based CPP, and (III) ayahuasca prevention of cocaine-induced CPP reinstatement. Test sessions = 15 min free exploration; conditioning sessions = 30 min. Outcomes: CPP score and difference score; tracking via EthoVision XT 11.5.

application_type.evidence: Ayahuasca administered by gavage (p.o.); cocaine administered i.p. (10 mg/kg)

setup_habituation.evidence: a habituation session and a preconditioning (preCT) test were performed on days 1 and 2, respectively, in which animals were placed in the center of the apparatus with the doors open with free access to both compartments for 15 min

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were placed in the center of the apparatus with free access to both compartments

food_restriction.evidence: food and water provided ad libitum in home cage; no food in CPP apparatus during testing

water_restriction.evidence: food and water provided ad libitum in home cage; no water in CPP apparatus during testing

time_to_assay.evidence: 30 min later, corresponding to the approximate onset of the psychedelic effects following oral ayahuasca administration, they were placed in the compartment paired with ayahuasca or water

sample_size.evidence: C57Bl/6 male mice (n = 93); Protocol I n = 10 per group; Protocol II n = 10; Protocol III n = 11 per group

outcomes.summary: Ayahuasca induced CPP only at the highest dose tested (15 mg DMT/kg), with a positive correlation between cumulative DMT dose and difference score. In a choice-based paradigm, cocaine (10 mg/kg) produced more pronounced CPP than ayahuasca. In the reinstatement protocol, ayahuasca treatment (12.5 or 15 mg DMT/kg) during withdrawal prevented the reinstatement of cocaine-induced CPP following a cocaine challenge.
outcomes.statistics: Protocol I: F(4,36)=2.306, p>0.05 interaction; F(4,45)=1.089, p<0.05 (difference score); Pearson r=0.1113, p<0.05. Protocol II: F(1,18)=26.52, p<0.0001 interaction; t(9)=3.650, p<0.01. Protocol III: F(6,54)=3.064, p<0.05 interaction; F(3,27)=10.75, p<0.0001 main effect of test day; post-hoc ayahuasca vs water at postREINST p<0.05.
outcomes.evidence: only the group conditioned with 15 mg DMT/kg ayahuasca showed a significant increase in CPP score in the post-conditioning test; ayahuasca treatment effectively prevented the cocaine-induced CPP reinstatement

B1_num_measures.evidence: CPP score and difference score were both calculated and reported

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total time in compartments reported per session; no within-session time-binning

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of transitions or behavioural sequences reported

B4_ethological.evidence: CPP measures zone preference time, not ethological behaviours

B5_social.evidence: Animals tested alone in CPP apparatus

B6_cognitive.evidence: Conditioned place preference (CPP) is a well-established model for assessing associative learning

B7_automated_classification.evidence: analyzed using the EthoVision XT 11.5 (position tracking)

B8_multivariate.evidence: k-means clustering analysis was performed in RStudio using the CPP scores from postCT, postTREAT, and postREINST as input variables

E1_environment_type.evidence: CPP test was conducted in rectangular box (44 × 14 × 14 cm) divided into three chambers

E2_shelter.evidence: Open CPP chambers with no enclosed refuge

E3_bedding.evidence: rod floor and grid floor; no bedding

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material in CPP apparatus

E6_spatial.evidence: divided into three chambers: two equal-sized end-chambers separated by a smaller middle chamber with two guillotine doors

E7_social_context.evidence: animals were placed in the center of the apparatus with free access to both compartments (alone)

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in CPP apparatus during testing

D1_continuity.evidence: preCT, postCT, postTREAT, and postREINST tests conducted on separate days

D2_session_duration.evidence: free access to both compartments for 15 min (test); each conditioning session lasted 30 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Recorded test days: preCT (day 2), postCT (day 11), postTREAT (day 20), postREINST (day 22) = 4 recording days for the CPP test trials

D4_baseline.evidence: preconditioning (preCT) test was performed on day 2 and data used in analysis

D5_followup.evidence: postTREAT and postREINST tests conducted days after last ayahuasca administration

judge_notes: All three candidates identified a single CPP assay spanning three protocols (dose-response, choice-based, reinstatement). Merged accordingly per rubric (same paradigm under different drug/manipulation conditions = 1 assay).
B1 set to 2 (2-3 measures): CPP score and difference score are both reported and analyzed as primary outcomes; chose modal value of 2 measures.

D2 set to 1 (15–60 min): longest recording session is the 30-min conditioning session, and conditioning data are reported (paired t-tests on baseline, etc.). Even ignoring conditioning, 15-min test sessions qualify under the inclusive boundary.

D3 set to 1 (2-7 days): counted the 4 distinct CPP test days where the freely-exploring preference data are reported. Conditioning days were not counted as separate test-data recording days for this scoring.
Housing fields kept as not_reported where the paper is silent; light cycle direction is explicitly standard (lights on 07:00) so day_night_flipped=no with high confidence.

Added cocaine to dosing context implicitly via experimental description but kept dosing block focused on the psychedelic (Ayahuasca) per rubric — cocaine is a comparator/reinstatement-inducing drug, not a psychedelic.
